tldr: ROCODE integrates a backtracking mechanism with program analysis into LLMs for code generation, detecting errors in real-time during generation and strategically rolling back to prevent error accumulation rather than revising after completion.
contributions: ROCODE: a novel model-agnostic code generation approach that integrates backtracking and program analysis to prevent error accumulation during LLM decoding
Incremental error detection using compiler-based program analysis on incomplete code (syntax, type, runtime, and repeat pattern errors)
Strategic rollback strategies that use error reports and model uncertainty (entropy) to determine optimal rollback points
Constraint regeneration with exponentially decaying penalties on erroneous token paths to avoid recurrence
Trie Tree modeling of non-linear code generation trajectories with rollbacks and regenerations
methods: ROCODE performs incremental error detection by running compiler-based program analysis after each generated statement to identify syntax, type, runtime, and repeat pattern errors. When an error is detected, a strategic rollback is triggered: either rolling back to the error's reported location or to the highest-entropy token position, determined via model uncertainty analysis. Constraint regeneration then applies exponentially decaying penalties (PN(v|y<t) = λ^(t-r)) to tokens on the erroneous path, and the entire process is modeled using a Trie Tree to manage non-linear generation trajectories.
results: ROCODE achieves a compilation pass rate of 99.1% and improves test pass rate by up to 23.8% compared to the best baseline. Token cost is reduced by 19.3% compared to post-revising baselines. It achieves a relative improvement of 34.2% in pass rate for multilingual code generation and an average improvement of 18.2% across nine representative LLMs. Ablation studies confirm that incremental error detection, rollback strategies, and constraint regeneration all contribute to performance improvement.
limitations: The paper does not explicitly discuss limitations. However, the approach may face challenges with complex semantic/dependency errors where the root cause is difficult to pinpoint, and the penalty-based constraint regeneration risks inadvertently suppressing benign tokens that share prefixes with erroneous paths.
